engineering_wire_validation_recipe: These JSON Schemas are engineering wire-checking contracts exercised by tests; the live runtime does not invoke a JSON Schema validator.
Reject duplicate JSON keys and non-JSON types before lossy serialization. Use an exact raw-integer type check at accepted typed-field boundaries; preserve rejected proposal payloads as evidence.
Validate the selected closed wire schema with local references resolved offline.
For each record, explicitly parse body_json and validate record_body_KIND as a separate engineering check; contentSchema annotations alone do not enforce this.
Wire-shape success is not runtime admission, mathematical verification, integrity validation or replay acceptance.

live_runtime_gates.typed_deserialization: Strict native dataclass parsers enforce accepted raw types, rational and identity bounds, immutable snapshots and bounded state. CanonicalRecord enforces a known kind, bounded canonical JSON body and content digest; it does not validate each body against record_body_KIND.
live_runtime_gates.transition_authority: The versioned coordinator constructs record bodies and enforces live issuer, scope, state, budget, qualification and mathematical checking gates.
live_runtime_gates.persisted_authority: replay_native_journal reconstructs every persisted transition and record through the coordinator under a caller-trusted genesis and complete journal digest; saved state and record bodies are never imported as authority.

trust_boundary: The Python host, source profile and externally retained complete journal anchor are trusted inputs. Hashes and role labels do not authenticate a principal.
non_claims: JSON Schema proves no mathematical truth or installation authority.
Canonical records are immutable evidence; semantic reference validation requires native replay.
A trace can retain rejected malformed proposals; accepted_intent is the separate admission shape.
No neural learning, arbitrary program synthesis, secret evaluation custody, external actions or full-machine completion.
